review_candidates.title: Product Manager - AI Community Wisdom
review_candidates.description: POSITION TITLE : Product Manager - AI Community Wisdom LOCATION: Kenya (Hybrid) POSITION TYPE : Fixed-term contract (12 months). 3-4 days per week. Working days to be agreed on appointment. ANNUAL PACKAGE : KES 230,000-280,000 monthly gross. Additional perks: - Internet stipend - Local co-working membership - Learning budget A budget is available to commission configuration and implementation work you scope and direct. REPORTS TO: Chief Executive Officer (CEO) DIRECT REPORTS: Program Coordinator ABOUT YGAP ygap believes that social entrepreneurship is a force for good. We back local innovators who understand their communities best, with the knowledge, community and capital to build sustainable impact ventures that help marginalised women and youth thrive. ygap operates in Kenya, Fiji and Australia and, since 2008 we have accelerated 817 locally-led impact ventures. ygap is committed to safeguarding the wellbeing of the youth and communities we work with. This role requires adherence to ygap's Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct. POSITION DESCRIPTION ygap is piloting a WhatsApp-based Community Voice tool: a low-bandwidth way for the people our innovators serve to give feedback through the channels they already use, and an AI layer that turns that feedback into insights innovators can rapidly act on. We plan to customise an existing no-code platform, shortlisted from a small number of proven options, and pilot it with three ygap innovators in Kenya whose social ventures reach thousands of smallholder farmers. We need someone who understands ground realities and can test whether thousands of Kiswahili voice notes and texts can surface real stories and actionable insights. You will customise technology into a three-sided product, serving: the farmer/end beneficiary who shares their challenges and successes, the innovator who holds the conversation and acts on what comes back, and ygap, which helps amplify community voices as evidence. You do not have to build the stack alone, configuration can be commissioned, and a budget is available for it. The right person will believe sitting with three innovators, earning their trust, and listening to their farmers/end beneficiary is the key to designing an impactful product. This is fundamentally a human-facing role. Key Objectives 1. By 45 days, you will have run discovery with the three ventures, learning what devices farmers/end beneficiary have, their data costs, how many a WhatsApp-only approach would exclude, and the digital and AI capability of each innovator and their team. This would inform your decision on proceeding with WhatsApp as the channel. 2. By 90 days, you will have defined the MVP users stories for the farmers/end beneficiary, innovators and ygap and used these to inform your choice of tech tools (WhatsApp service, Kiswahili speech layer, sense making, data management). 3. By 120 days, you will have the first data flows live with a small test group on your MVP solution, and be preparing to expand across the three social ventures according to your deployment plan designed in consultation with the innovators. 4. Over 9 months, refine the product and set up all three social ventures to own and run their own feedback loops independently. RESPONSIBILITIES & DUTIES Innovator and Community Engagement - Build the relationships that make this work possible. Three innovators have to want this, and have to trust the person asking them to try it. - Triage the needs of the three innovators and the communities they serve, and translate what you hear into a solution that will actually land. - Spend time with smallholder farmers/end beneficiary directly. Test assumptions with them rather than about them. - Deliver hands-on coaching to support innovators in creating efficiencies in their social ventures through AI. Tech Stack Decisions and Implementation - Run user research across all three ventures to validate or falsify the central hypothesis: we expect farmers/end users will engage with MEL activities via WhatsApp. - Select the Kiswahili speech layer separately from the platform, testing candidate models against real field audio rather than benchmark audio. - Write clear, specific briefs for implementation partners or contractors to configure the stack, and direct that work to completion. Configure directly where doing it yourself is faster. You are accountable for the result either way. - Pilot every flow with a small group of farmers/end beneficiary and refine before going wide. Sense-making, Analysis and Reporting - Design the system that turns thousands of unstructured voice notes and messages into patterns someone can act on. Most of this is orchestrating AI well: defining the parameters, the prompts and the checks, then letting it do the heavy lifting. Far less of it is spreadsheets and formulas. - Guard against false confidence. Kiswahili speech recognition is imperfect and AI summaries read as fluent whether or not they are right. Build in verification and be able to explain where a finding came from. Team and Sector Contribution - Manage, support and develop the Program Coordinator. SUCCESS METRICS - In-field testing of tools and innovator digital capability documented for all three ventures within 45 days - Three innovators actively engaged and willing to keep going, evidenced by their own feedback - At least 500 farmer/end beneficiary and innovator interactions processed through the tech stack during the pilot period - Three ventures running their own feedback loops - Documented changes made by social ventures as a direct result of farmer/end beneficiary feedback - Consent, privacy and data residency position in place and adhered to KEY SELECTION CRITERIA Essential. - Demonstrated ability to build trust with innovators and coach them to adopt new technology in their social ventures. This is the largest part of the role and the first bar you have to clear. - Kiswahili fluency, and a working understanding of Kenyan ground realities in rural and low-resource contexts. Confidence in additional Kenyan languages will strengthen an application. - Strong strategic thinking and synthesis. Able to sit with messy, conflicting input from founders and communities and come back with a clear position on what to build and why. - Ability to orchestrate AI to make sense of unstructured data. We are not looking for a data analytics specialist. We are looking for someone who can define a system and its parameters, direct AI to do the heavy lifting, and know when the output is wrong. - Ability to write a clear, specific technical brief and hold a contractor to it. You will direct configuration work, not necessarily do all of it. - Comfort in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, with the ability to project manage, prioritise and execute with attention to detail. - Strong alignment with ygap's mission and values. An adaptive, ownership mindset. - Permanently authorised to work in Kenya. Valuable, and we will support you if you do not have it yet. - A working ethical position on AI in low-resource contexts. Specifically: who owns data collected from people with little power, what informed consent means when the person consenting has not used a chatbot before, and what to do when a model performs worse for some speakers than others. - Impact measurement and MEL grounding, including how to design indicators and surveys. - Experience managing a team member or contractors. Remote and cross-timezone management is an advantage. We hire for disposition as much as experience. If you meet the essential criteria and only some of the second list, please apply. This is not a software engineering role and you will not write production code. APPLICATION PROCESS Please send an email to careers@ygap.org including: 1. A short video (maximum 3 minutes) responding to the case study below. Record it on your phone. We are not assessing production quality. If bandwidth is a constraint, a WhatsApp voice note is equally welcome. Case study One of our innovators runs an agricultural venture in Kiambu county. She works with 600 smallholder farmers engaged in beekeeping, mostly women and youth. Her team of five field officers visit farmer groups monthly, training and supplying bee keeping equipment on credit and buying produce back at an agreed price. Most farmers have basic smartphones. WhatsApp use is common but not universal, and many prefer sending voice notes to typing. She wants to understand three things: why some farmer groups continue working with her while others drop off, whether farmers feel her equipment and services are fairly priced, and what would encourage farmers who have stopped selling their honey to her to return. Talk us through how you would approach gathering that. Include the five questions you would ask a farmer by WhatsApp voice note or text in Kiswahili, and why you chose those five and not others. 2. One artefact, plus no more than half a page. Either a screenshot of a no-code flow or dashboard you have built, or an example of how you have used AI to make sense of messy, unstructured information. Tell us what it was for, who used it, and what you got wrong the first time. We are looking at how you think, not at the data. 3. Your CV. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. We aim to have the successful candidate start in October 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to talk through their thinking live with ygap and a technology advisor. We are interested in how you reason, not how well you present.
